A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same StrandHead study, with complete main text, references and supplementary Sections 6.1–6.6. Comparison of all 20 pages, including text, equations, tables, figures and embedded resources, establishes no material gaps.

before.justification: v3 reports original head and hair generation experiments, quantitative comparisons and a user study in Section 4 and Table 2, plus supplementary evaluations and ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments, user-study outcomes, quantitative results and supplementary analyses, including Tables 2–3.

M1.justification: The three-stage generation pipeline, FLAME-evolving prior, differentiable prismatization, geometric regularizers and strand-aware texture field are identical in Sections 3 and 6.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same USC-HairSalon data, head and hair generation tasks, prompt list, and test scenarios varying hairstyle descriptions and bald heads. No dataset or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 2–3 is identical, including TECA in both generation tasks and HAAR in hair generation. The NeuralHaircut quad-mesh comparison in Figures 3 and 15 is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain 30 prompts per generation task, BLIP/BLIP2-VQA evaluation, and a user study using 10 examples and 30 volunteers. Supplementary FID/CLIP protocols, training budgets and ablation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The same prior/loss and texture-field ablations, strand-count and prism-parameter sensitivity analyses, metric comparison, nearest-hairstyle retrieval check, failure cases and conditioning tests appear in both versions.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical, including point estimates, user-preference percentages and hairstyle distributions. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 2–3 and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, StrandHead's head/hair FID remains 176.95/201.19, and its generation-quality preference remains 53.67%/57.67%.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(23), mathematical definitions, loss formulations and the prismatization construction are identical. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same novelty and performance claims concerning text-driven strand generation using human-centric priors, avoidance of large-scale paired supervision, and support for editing, transfer and simulation.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations of prior-guided generation, CLIP-metric limitations and generation versus retrieval. Limitations concerning complex hairstyles and high SDS computational cost are unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures are identical, including loss weights, iteration budgets, 3,000 strands with 100 points each, A6000 hardware, runtime and memory requirements. Project-page access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, 94 references and positioning relative to methods such as HumanNorm, TECA and HAAR are identical. No cited works are added or removed.

P1.justification: Only the first-page marginal arXiv stamp changes from v3 dated 26 Jul 2025 to v4 dated 14 Feb 2026. The title, authors, prose, terminology and section structure remain identical.

P2.justification: All 25 figures, three tables, captions and page arrangements are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–20 match exactly; the first-page difference is confined to the version/date stamp text.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information, limitations and presentation are unchanged throughout the main text and supplement. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp and its link provides no meaningful improvement or deterioration in paper quality.
